per_view.notes: Plain grey cylinder ~10x diameter with blunt rounded ends, no nose taper. No engines, no hump, no landing gear, no windows. One dark unswept rectangular slab at rear top as fin; no horizontal stabilizers. Thin dark strip mid-body may be an edge-on flat wing. Muted grey/navy but featureless; barely reads as aircraft.

Plain light-grey cylinder with blunt rounded ends, no nose taper or tail cone. One unswept dark rectangular slab on the tail top (crude fin), no horizontal stabilizers. A small dark trapezoid on the lower mid-body vaguely hints at a wing root. No engines, hump, gear, windows, or doors. Parts join cleanly but assembly is minimal.

Plain constant-diameter cylinder fuselage with blunt ends; single unswept untapered rectangular wing slab at 90 degrees; no engines, pylons, or hump visible in planform; no horizontal stabilizers, only a thin edge-on fin sliver past the tail; two-tone grey scheme; assembly is clean but reads as a plus-sign, not a 747.

Plain grey cylinder with blunt flat ends, no nose taper or tail cone. Two flat, untapered, unswept dark slab wings, no dihedral. Single rectangular vertical fin floats with a visible gap above the fuselage; no horizontal stabilizers. No engines, hump, windows, or surface detail. Reads as a generic toy plane.

Plain gray cylinder with blunt rounded ends; no nose taper. One flat dark swept plate sits atop the rear fuselage, a small plate hangs below mid-body, and a single rectangular fin rises at the rear. No engines, no hump, no landing gear, no windows. Parts read as thin floating slabs.

critic.fix_suggestion: Improve 'Four engines under swept wings' (mean 0/10). Target the 8 anchor: four nacelles hung under the swept wings on visible pylons, plausible inboard/outboard spacing; then the 10 anchor: four underslung pylon-mounted nacelles with correct relative size, spacing, and forward offset ahead of the wing leading edge, inlet visibly open/darker.
